Живут они от 1 до 12 часов — это их TTL (time to live, срок жизни).

patterns: Each acronym is expanded at most once in the whole zone and then treated as global knowledge, but the reader arrives at files out of order. S3 is expanded only in 02, RDS only in 08, ECS only in 09, ALB only in 04 (and there only in the last section, after two earlier uses), IAM only in 05, GSI only in 08/11 — while EC2, ARN, ACM, ENI, OAC, TTL, RCU/WCU, HA, CAPEX/OPEX, ACID, SLA, SPA, RPS, DLQ, P99 are never expanded in any of the 22 files in either locale. The result is 5-16 cold acronyms per article and 23+ in 11-aws-interview-questions. This is the zone's dominant defect and it is identical in ru and en.

Roughly 60% of H2 sections open directly with a fenced ```txt or code block and no orienting sentence — no statement of what the block shows or what to conclude from it. Worst: 10-aws-architecture-patterns (9 of 10 sections, including all seven `Pattern N` sections in a row), 03-lambda-and-serverless (7 of 8), 05-iam-security (6 of 7), 09-ecs-fargate-containers (5 of 7). Where a lead sentence does exist it is good and does answer first (02's Pre-Signed URL section is the model to copy), so this is a missing-habit problem, not a writing-skill problem.

The RU locale is not bureaucratic (almost no «является»/«осуществляется»/«данный») but it is heavily code-switched: English terms are dropped into Russian clauses undeclined and sometimes replace the Russian word entirely — «sporadic трафик», «predictable трафик», «Стоишь при zero трафике», «механизм evaluation», «Lifecycle Lambda функции», «managed NoSQL БД». Where the switch is done carelessly the text becomes factually wrong: «состояния машин» for state machines (06), «low-latency latency» (08), «трacing» (04), «нет DevOps» where EN says "no DevOps overhead" (01). Nearly every H2 in the RU files is an untranslated English phrase, and 10 and 11 have untranslated H1s.

CDK snippets reference identifiers that are created in a different section or never created at all: `distribution` (02, 05), `iam` and `ec2` namespaces with no import (02, 03), `Duration` with no import (09), `vpc`, `dbSecret`, `bucket`, `table`, `handler`, `api`, `acmCertificate`, `sendEmail`, `db`. No single snippet in the zone outside 01 can be read to the end without an unresolved name, which makes the code examples reference material rather than something a reader can follow.

EN is the *easier* locale here, not the harder one — it carries none of the code-switching, and its bullets read cleanly at B1-B2. Its only real penalty is sentence length in the `Common interview mistakes` lists, where a quoted myth + rebuttal + numeric caveat are packed into one 28-37-word sentence (05: two at 32w; 08: one at 36w; 10: leads at 37w and 35w). The RU equivalents of those same bullets are shorter because Russian drops the connectives — so the standard fix (split at the em-dash into myth sentence / correction sentence / caveat sentence) is needed in EN only.
notes: Three concrete bugs a language pass should sweep, all RU-only: «в всех регионах» (01, l.48), «→ CDK deploy (или cdk deploy)» (10, l.176, the EN file already dropped the duplicate), and register inconsistency — 01/02 address the reader as «Вы управляете», 09 switches to «Ты управляешь/Ты платишь». Emphasis is done with ALL-CAPS words inside prose in both locales (ОДНОГО, ВСЕМ, ДОЛЖНЫ / MUST, BEFORE, THE SAME); bold or italics would read better on a phone and would stop tripping the abbreviation scanner. RU files carry a `<!-- verified: 2026-06-05 -->` header that the EN files lack. Files 06 and 07 are the zone's best work in both locales (every concept gets a before/after diagram) and are the right internal model for the rest.
